critical_operation.description: doGenerate() encodes "." and ".." path segments so a generated URL still resolves to its route after RFC 3986 §5.2.4 dot-segment removal. critical_operation.description: The free template function google::protobuf::internal::ParseMessageSetItemImpl (not a WireFormatLite member) tracks MessageSet progress with two sentinel values rather than a state machine. last_type_id == 0 means 'no type id seen', and message_data.empty() means 'no buffered payload'; a real type id of 0 is indistinguishable from 'unset'. Message tags are either buffered when last_type_id is 0 or parsed immediately into the extension when it is non-zero. The parser never records that a type id/payload pair was already completed, so duplicate type-id and duplicate message tags in one MessageSetItem are accepted and the same logical field is parsed or merged repeatedly instead of being rejected or skipped. The fix replaces the sentinels with enum class State { kNoTag, kHasType, kHasPayload, kDone } and, in the terminal state, skips duplicate payload bytes instead of re-parsing them. The same design appears in WireFormat::MessageSetParser (wire_format.cc) and ExtensionSet::ParseMessageSetItemTmpl (extension_set_inl.h); the fix patches all three.

critical_operation.description: The signing salt is built by string concatenation: signing.get_cookie_signer(salt=key + salt). The pair (name='a', salt='bc') and (name='ab', salt='c') both yield 'abc', so a cookie signed for one context verifies in the other. set_signed_cookie in django/http/response.py uses the same concatenation on the write path.

entry_point.description: Application code calls django.http.HttpRequest.get_signed_cookie(key, salt=...) to read a signed cookie. The same concatenation is used on the write path, HttpResponseBase.set_signed_cookie(key, value, salt=...).

root_cause: Non-injective salt derivation: concatenating cookie name and salt without a length/domain separator makes distinct (name, salt) pairs collide.

trace.description: get_signed_cookie reads the cookie value named key from request.COOKIES and, when absent, returns the default or re-raises.
Line 191 derives the signer salt as key + salt and unsigns the cookie value with it; the derivation is injective only if no two (name, salt) pairs concatenate to the same string.
get_cookie_signer passes that string as the Signer salt; Signer.salt is salted_hmac's key prefix, so equal salts mean equal MAC namespaces.
The write path mirrors the read path: set_signed_cookie signs with signing.get_cookie_signer(salt=key + salt).

Fixed releases instead use signing._cookie_signer_salt(), returning 'django.http.cookies.v2:<len(salt)>:<salt><cookie_name>', and keep accepting legacy cookies only while SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK is True (default on 5.2.15/6.0.6, False on 6.1).

The pattern is unanchored, so the engine restarts it at every offset where the literal can begin; each attempt runs greedy (.*) to the end of its line and then backtracks looking for a CRLF followed by a non-whitespace character. A single occurrence is therefore one linear scan; the quadratic case needs many occurrences in the same header line and no CRLF+non-space after them, e.g. a line built from repeated 'Content-Disposition:' tokens followed by a folded continuation line that starts with a space, which makes the lookahead fail at the end of the long line. Line 311 tests disposition.bytesize <= CONTENT_DISPOSITION_MAX_BYTES (1536, defined at 305) only after the match, so the cap does not bound that work.
